title: Integral compact support under finite free coefficient extension
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with their valuation rings and uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $e=e(F/E)\geq1$ be the ramification index, defined by $\varpi_E\mathcal O_F=\varpi_F^e\mathcal O_F$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. On each small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and define $C_W(M)=M\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ by ordinary derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Work in the derived-complete integral constructible categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and their uniform finite-Tor subcategories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Use the integral compact-support functors $P_E=Rf_{!,E}$ and $P_F=Rf_{!,F}$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. On the domain $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$c_{F/E}:C_Y P_E\xrightarrow{\sim}P_F C_X.$$
For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the displayed component has source $C_Y(P_EM)$ and target $P_F(C_XM)$. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$, with $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For every integer $n\geq1$, put $A_n=A_{E,n}$, $B_n=A_{F,en}$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$, and $C_W^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W$ for $W=X,\overline X,Y$. Under the cofinal strict reduction-tower presentations of the integral compact-support functors, $c_{F/E,M}$ is induced by the compatible finite coefficient tensor comparisons whose ordered composite at level $n$ is
$$C_Y^{(n)}Rp_{*,A_n}j_!M_n\longrightarrow Rp_{*,B_n}C_{\overline X}^{(n)}j_!M_n\longrightarrow Rp_{*,B_n}j_!C_X^{(n)}M_n.$$
Here $j_!$ is finite-coefficient extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero], $Rp_{*,A_n}$ and $Rp_{*,B_n}$ are separately derived proper direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image], the first arrow is the canonical proper direct-image coefficient tensor map and the second is the canonical open coefficient identification. These maps are compatible on the strict reduction towers before taking derived limits. Its reduction modulo $(\varpi_E^n)S=(\varpi_F^{en})$, for every $n\geq1$, is the same finite-free compact-support comparison for $A_{E,n}\to A_{F,en}$, and it commutes with further quotient reductions. It intertwines the compact-support projection transformations [def-exchange-projection] with scalar extension, and commutes with the canonical shift comparisons. It is independent of the chosen compactification, with the refinement normalizations of the compact-support definition. For $F=E$ it is identity under $C_W\cong1$. If $E\subset F\subset L$, and $\alpha^W:C_{L/F,W}C_{F/E,W}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_{L/E,W}$ is ordinary tensor associativity, its composition law is
$$c_{L/E,M}\circ\alpha^Y_{P_EM}=P_L(\alpha^X_M)\circ c_{L/F,C_{F/E,X}M}\circ C_{L/F,Y}(c_{F/E,M}).$$
All assertions concern these specified comparisons on the constructible finite-Tor domain, and use ordinary tensor presentations identified with strict-tower scalar extension by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. No smoothness or purity hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Step 3, coefficient-extension transport: implicit compact-support coefficient comparison used when taking the adjunction mate. Agent auxiliary; construction supported by Bhatt-Scholze Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.7 (separately derived compact-support composite), Lemma 6.8.2(1) (completed coefficients), and the finite-free tensor/strict-tower constructions.
source.note: No numbered result of Bhatt-Scholze or Stacks is claimed to state this full varying-coefficient coherence. The node isolates the required independent compact-support comparison, without any smooth purity map or exceptional comparison in its conclusion.

proof.text: Write $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_F$. The equality of ideals $t\mathcal O_F=v^e\mathcal O_F$ in the hypothesis gives $t^n\mathcal O_F=v^{en}\mathcal O_F$, without identifying the two chosen uniformizers. In particular $B_n=\mathcal O_F/t^n\mathcal O_F=A_{F,en}$ is finite free over $A_n$ by [lem-coef-finite-free-extension]. We will also use a single integral basis, only to check invertibility of intrinsically defined maps. Here is its justification. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete], $\mathcal O_E$ is $t$-adically complete: lift a compatible system of residues to $a_n\in\mathcal O_E$ with $a_{n+1}-a_n\in t^n\mathcal O_E$. This sequence is Cauchy in $E$; its limit stays in the closed unit ball and in each closed residue ball $a_n+t^n\mathcal O_E$, so gives the required lift. Injectivity follows from $|t|_E^n\to0$. The same valuation calculation in $F$ gives $\bigcap_n t^n\mathcal O_F=0$. The finite module $B_1$ is finitely generated over $A_1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] to $\mathcal O_F$ as an $\mathcal O_E$-module. It is finite and torsion free, since $E\subset F$ are fields. [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] therefore supplies an $\mathcal O_E$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $\mathcal O_F$. This basis induces compatible bases of every $B_n$ over $A_n$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), completed coefficients; elementary valuation-ring argument using the cited arithmetic statements

proof.text: Keep completed and constant integral coefficient sheaves distinct. [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] gives finite freeness of $S_W$ over $R_W$, derived $v$-completeness of $C_WK$, and the specified ordinary-tensor/strict-tower isomorphism $\chi$. [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies the derived-complete completed-coefficient category with the derived-complete category for the discrete constant ring sheaf $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$; it identifies quotient tensors, their transition maps and their strict derived limits. The same applies to $F$. In this model scalar extension on reduction towers is tensor with $\underline{\mathcal O_F}$, whose underlying $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$-module is the finite direct sum with basis from Step 1. At level $n$ it sends $M_n$ to $M_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}(B_n)_X$, canonically identified with $C_XM\otimes^L_{S_X}(B_n)_X$ by tensor balancing on the K-flat models of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The coefficient inverse-image identifications for scheme maps, both finite and completed, commute with these quotient maps by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Thus all ringed squares used below have commuting structure-ring maps. For the ambient tensor model use the native derived localization tensor and its natural K-flat representative comparison [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]; this constructs tensorModel_exists without a new existence assumption.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1); completion and finite reductions, Proposition 3.5.1; Stacks Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat

proof.text: Define the proper coefficient comparison for $p$ to be the adjunction mate of the canonical pullback/scalar tensor comparison. Explicitly its transpose is $p_B^*C_Y^{(n)}Rp_{*,A}N\cong C_{\overline X}^{(n)}p_A^*Rp_{*,A}N\xrightarrow{C^{(n)}\varepsilon_{p,A}}C_{\overline X}^{(n)}N$. The derived ringed adjunction, tensor comparison and counit-defined projection map are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Upon restriction to $A$ its value is the projection map followed by the direct-image/restriction identification of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction]. Because $B_n$ is free of rank $r$, this restricted projection is the biproduct comparison $(Rp_{*,A}N)^{\oplus r}\to Rp_{*,A}(N^{\oplus r})$. It is invertible: an additive functor sends the biproduct injections and projections to injections and projections satisfying the same matrix identities. Restriction reflects isomorphisms by the same cited change-of-ring lemma. For the open constituent use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] and the exactness of open extension in [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; tensor with finite free $B_n$ is exact, so its ordinary tensor is its derived tensor. This gives $C_{\overline X}^{(n)}j_!\cong j_!C_X^{(n)}$. Compose these two specified maps, in the order in the statement, to obtain the finite comparison $q_n$. This construction does not assume purity. The equality of the ordered factorization is the vertical-pasting identity mateEquiv_vcomp, applied before asserting any factor is invertible.

Construct the comparison before taking limits. Let $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Use the small ringed diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], initially with the constant rings $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ and $\underline{\mathcal O_F}$. For a K-flat representative of $M$, its quotient maps give a strict diagram of reductions. Replacements are made in the diagram category, using [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements], not independently at its objects. The compact-support diagram is the separately derived proper image after exact open extension; [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] supplies precisely this exact lift and its coefficient-restriction transitions. On the diagram sites form the proper scalar mate of Step 3, with tensor by the constant $\underline{\mathcal O_F}$, and the open tensor comparison. The derived adjunction and projection construction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] applies to these small ringed sites. This defines one transformation $q_\bullet$ in the derived category of strict towers. [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective] identifies evaluation of the separately derived proper part with its proper derived image at that level. [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] identifies its finite coefficient actions and adjunction transposes. Its evaluation is therefore exactly $q_n$, not merely some isomorphism with the same source and target. Transition compatibility follows already in this construction: a quotient acts on a tensor by $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\bar b$; this commutes with the open tensor map and the counit transpose defining the proper map. The diagram sites also retain the $\mathcal O_F$-action throughout.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), diagram site; Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and Tag 0B56, applied on that site

proof.text: Take total derived inverse limit of the strict map $q_\bullet$ of Step 4, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The exact countable products supplied by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] identify this functor with the specified product/cone model by [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Apply [lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality] in the constant coefficient models of Step 2: finite free tensor commutes with this cone, and its explicit block map identifies the full $F$-tower limit with the retained $en$-tower limit. Both comparisons preserve the augmentation and the coefficient action. The integral definition [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and the specified scalar map $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] therefore give $c_{F/E}$ with the required source and target. Each $q_n$ is invertible, so its tower cone has zero cohomology at every level. Cohomology of towers is levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; the cone is zero before taking limits. The exact total-limit functor makes $c_{F/E}$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), Roos complex; finite-block cone elimination and finite direct-sum calculation

proof.text: Check reduction of this specified map. The $E$-compact-support tower is normalized: derived reduction of $M$ is normalized by tensor associativity, and [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] makes its compact-support image normalized for every $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$, compatibly with successive reductions. For the full $F$-tower use the same finite coefficient-change theorem with coefficient field $F$ and all quotients $A_{F,b}\to A_{F,a}$. The finite-Tor condition on $C_XM$ required there follows from the independent tensor calculation in Step 7. The quotient adjoints and their cocycles, together with the strict lifts of Step 4, give exactly the normalized towers of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to the full $t$-tower for $E$ and the full $v$-tower for $F$, and then restrict the latter limit projections to the indices $en$ using Step 5. This uses $v$, rather than $t$, as the uniformizer of $\mathcal O_F$. The adjunction of [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] identifies the adjoints of the limit projections with the canonical finite reductions of $P_E M$ and $P_FC_XM$. Since the product/cone maps of Step 5 commute with those projections, reduction of $c_{F/E,M}$ modulo $t^nS$ is exactly $q_n$. Every further quotient square commutes already on the strict quotient complexes of Step 4, so it remains commutative under these adjoint reduction identifications. This proves the reduction clause as an equality of the specified finite maps; it makes no assertion that reductions determine arbitrary integral morphisms. The two coefficient-square comparison equations follow formally from comparison_composition on the two paths, cancelling the common tensor associator. The quotient ring squares themselves are checked by quotient induction; inverse-image compatibility is proEtaleConstantInverseImageMap_naturality.

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings); normalized-tower effectivity and adjunction with reduction

proof.text: All functors just used are defined on the asserted domain. [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] carries integral bounded constructible objects to integral bounded constructible objects, and [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies this functor with $C_X$. For any $F$-level $a$, choose $n$ with $en\geq a$. Tensor associativity gives $(C_XM)_a\cong M_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{F,a}$. For a degree-zero $A_{F,a}$-module $N$, tensoring once more gives $M_n\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}N$, with $N$ restricted to $A_{E,n}$. The uniform Tor bounds for $M$ therefore give the same bounds at every $a$, by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Thus $C_XM$ lies in the required finite-Tor category. [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] gives the bounded constructible integral outputs $P_EM$ and $P_FC_XM$ to which the ordinary/complete comparison applies. No smoothness or exceptional adjoint is used in this typing argument.

source.place: Definition 6.7.6 and Lemma 6.7.7; scalar-extension typing and elementary Tor-bound calculation

proof.text: Check refinement independence in the strict model. The finite reductions are bounded below and of etale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. Restrict the integral reduction towers to constant $\mathcal O_E$ or $\mathcal O_F$ using [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The normalized proper/open comparisons on these strict tower categories are precisely those of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. That statement applies to arbitrary constant rings, and its hypotheses only require each evaluated complex to have a bounded-below finite-coefficient etale-origin witness, which was just checked. For a refinement its pullback map is the clopen projection described there, followed by its proper-adjunction mate. Tensoring by the finite free $\mathcal O_F$ carries that projection to itself: on the section component it is identity and on its complementary component it is zero, separately on each basis coordinate. The open tensor comparison has the same property. Mate pasting [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], together with the counit definition in Step 3, shows that the resulting proper/open refinement square commutes with $q_\bullet$. These are identities on the diagram-site adjunctions, prior to evaluation. The strict proper/open composition laws and the common refinements of [prop-compactification-refinement] identify the comparisons for any two compactifications, with the identity and cocycle normalizations. Applying derived limit and the completed-coefficient equivalence proves the asserted compactification independence of $c$.

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), 0F7C and 0F7D (vertical and horizontal composition); normalized strict-tower version of the cited calculus

proof.text: First check the finite projection square of [def-exchange-projection]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the square whose horizontal maps are identity-topos coefficient changes $A_n\to B_n$ and whose vertical maps are $p$. The ring maps commute by Step 2. Its exchange is the proper coefficient mate of Step 3, so the stated equality is the required proper square. For the open constituent, both composites send $((x\otimes b)\otimes(y\otimes b'))$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes bb'$. This includes the zero sections of extension by zero; the equality descends through sheafification. [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] identifies these maps with the canonical open tensor maps.

For the integral square work in the constant coefficient model of Step 2. Apply [lem-pur-compact-support-completed-projection-coherence] with $A=\mathcal O_E$ and then $\mathcal O_F$. The completion reflector and its induced pullback adjunction are [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction]. The quotient $A/(\varpi^n)$ is perfect by its two-term free resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A]$. The open map is quasi-compact: over affine $V\subset\overline X$, its graph realizes $j^{-1}V$ as a closed subscheme of $X\times_kV$, a quasi-compact scheme. Thus [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] makes $j_!M$ complete and identifies it with its strict reduction limit. [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] then identifies integral compact support with $Rp_*j_!$. The new coherence lemma identifies the tower projection and counit with their completed-adjunction maps under precisely these limit comparisons. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the ordinary constant-ring square $\mathcal O_E\to\mathcal O_F$, and use the open balancing equality of the preceding step. Finite free tensor preserves the completion unit by Step 5; its constructible tensor and pullback comparisons are [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. The new lemma's unit equation makes both proposed completed composites equal after precomposition with that unit. Their target is complete, so its reflector Hom-bijection proves equality of the actual integral maps. No faithfulness of finite reductions is used.

For $E\subset F\subset L$, choose for the calculation the cofinal levels $A_{E,n}$, $A_{F,e(F/E)n}$ and $A_{L,e(L/F)e(F/E)n}$. The ideal equalities in Step 1 show that these are exactly reductions by the same power of $\varpi_E$. On the K-flat diagram representatives computing [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] the two pullback/coefficient associators send $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)$ to $x\otimes bc$. Thus their equality is an equality of the underlying pullback squares. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] makes the mate of their pasted square the composite of the two proper coefficient mates. For the open comparisons the same displayed balancing formula proves the composition equality directly. Substituting these identities into the ordered composite of Step 3 gives, already for the strict tower transformations,
$$q_{L/E}\alpha^Y=P_L(\alpha^X)\,q_{L/F}\,C_{L/F,Y}(q_{F/E}).$$
Apply the functorial product/cone comparison of Step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its maps use the very same balancing formula, so this equality becomes precisely the composition law for $c$ in the statement, with component $M$ and the displayed source $C_{L/F,Y}C_{F/E,Y}P_EM$. For the identity extension the pullback square is identity, its mate is identity by clause (4) of the same lemma, and the open tensor map is multiplication $x\otimes1\mapsto x$. Hence $c_{E/E}=1$ under the tensor-unit identifications. The completed ring maps respect identity and composition by their unique finite-residue normalization; the residue-map identities are proved on quotient representatives.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), units/counits and composite adjunctions; elementary tensor balancing on strict diagram representatives

proof.text: For the proper coefficient mate, apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift] on the original ringed sites and on the small diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Its counit equation identifies the transpose at $N[1]$ with $(C\varepsilon_N)[1]:C(p^*Rp_*N)[1]\to(CN)[1]$, the shift of the transpose at $N$. The pullback/scalar comparison is tensor balancing with the degree-zero algebra, hence has no first-variable sign. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom-bijection gives the proper mate's shift equation. For the open constituent use exact degreewise extension by zero [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]: on a representing complex both routes send $x\otimes b$ to $x\otimes b$, and shifting puts the same minus sign on the differential. Their ordered composite $q_\bullet$ therefore commutes with shift before taking limits. The compact-support lifts have the exact shift structures of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], and total limit is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Its comparison consequently respects these canonical shifts. Normalize scalar shifts directly by [lem-pur-right-kan-extension-coherent-shift] applied to the universal derived scalar counit; postcomposition by each shift equivalence preserves its Kan extension, so Kan uniqueness also proves uniqueness of this normalization.

source.place: Tags 06YU (definition-derived-tor), 0B56 (projection map), 0941 (strict derived limit); exact open extension, sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ

proof.text: Finally the strict scalar functor commutes with shift by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. On a K-flat representative the ordinary/strict comparison $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] is its quotient product map together with zero in the shifted product. Shifting this pair gives the quotient product map for the shifted complex; any cone sign acts on a zero extra component. Thus $\chi$ itself respects the specified shift structures, and the ordinary-tensor comparison $c_{F/E}$ has the shift compatibility just proved for its strict-tower realization. This completes the asserted compatibilities.

The statement, stmt_deps and Lean record are unchanged; the repair replaces the old steps 5, 9 and 11 with the new steps 5, 9-10 and 12-13. lem-pur-compact-support-roos-cofinality is true. The telescoping identity b_e(1-s)=(1-s_e)a_e holds. The map is degreewise split surjective, and 1-s is bijective between the kernels (solve backwards from each retained zero; the initial block is free), so it is a quasi-isomorphism even without exact products. The cases e=1, a zero tower, a constant tower, composition of restrictions, and rank 0 or 1 for the finite free tensor all check. lem-pur-compact-support-completed-projection-coherence is true: the unit equation is the reflector computation, its target is complete because Ru_* preserves complete objects, and the tower identification follows from the projection formula for perfect A/I^n together with 0A07. Its hypotheses (Noetherian ring, perfect quotients) hold for O_E and O_F with I=(uniformizer). It is the projection analogue of lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison, not a duplicate of it. Neither new node restates a clause of the item. The step citations match their uses, there is no cycle, and every dependency is on the unit's route.
